claim_being_audited: That the model can be certified for launch now, based on aggregate readiness and rehearsal results, if the packet documents the unresolved logistics customs triage limitation and monitoring commitment.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence satisfies the policy threshold for certification.
A weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case.
Product labels such as 'non-core' or low-volume do not resolve materiality when named customer commitments are implicated or legal review is pending.
For a material limitation affecting a named launch use case, disclosure or approved risk acceptance must exist before launch.
Aggregate readiness evidence can support launch readiness, but it cannot override an unmet mandatory disclosure or risk-acceptance condition.
evidence_requests: Final legal determination on whether the logistics customs triage gap must be disclosed before launch.
Evidence that the limitation has been disclosed in the required launch/model-card materials for the named use case or contractual customers.
Evidence of an approved risk acceptance covering this material limitation before launch.
Any admissible record showing the affected segment is not in fact a named launch use case or contractual customer segment, if that is being asserted.
specific_concerns: Admissible evidence establishes a segment-specific performance gap in logistics customs triage and that this segment is named in two freight customer commitments.
The governing policy says a weakness is material when it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case; product's 'non-core' label does not resolve materiality in that circumstance.
The release policy requires disclosure or approved risk acceptance before launch for material limitations affecting named launch use cases.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required is still open, so a required policy predicate remains unresolved at the time of certification.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support overall readiness but do not satisfy the separate disclosure/risk-acceptance requirement for a material limitation.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently defensible merely as a narrow aggregate-readiness decision with documentation of the gap.
That public model-card and AI-risk-management guidance provides sufficient support for certifying despite an unresolved internal policy requirement.
That documenting the limitation and monitoring commitment alone is enough absent evidence of disclosure completion or approved risk acceptance.
